9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, slightly above, Scarlett (Image 2) pauses at the crosswalk with her black coat lifting in the wind, phone still in her hand as the signal changes., Side-profile tracking composition keeps Scarlett (Image 2) centered on the crosswalk, with white stripes leading through frame and glass towers and yellow taxis streaking behind her., EXT. DOWNTOWN SIDEWALK — MORNING. Scarlett (Image 2) bursts from a narrow apartment entrance into a moving crowd, one hand holding a coffee and the other gripping her phone. The camera tracks backward at street level as taxis slide through the background and her coral lips flash when she calls, “Sorry—coming through!”, morning, downtown_sidewalk_glass_towers_yellow_taxis, Clear morning daylight with bright ambient exposure and crisp reflections in the glass towers. A direct on-camera flash briefly freezes Scarlett (Image 2) and the flower vendor (Image 3) at the kiosk., Cool gray pavement, reflective blue-gray glass, black clothing, white crosswalk stripes, yellow taxis, fresh green stems, and vivid coral flowers and lipstick., scarlett_city_influencer, vendor_flower_kiosk, Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
